question.text: What is the purpose of the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR)?

answer.text: To serve as a centralized repository for KYC records, de-duplicate client data, and issue a unique KYC Identifier to avoid repeated KYC submissions
To directly investigate suspicious transactions reported by financial institutions
To issue licenses and registrations to new reporting entities under PMLA
To maintain criminal records of all individuals convicted under PMLA

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the IFSCA workbook (pp.43, 44, 54), the Central KYC Records Registry receives, stores, safeguards and retrieves KYC records, processes them for de-duplication, and issues a unique KYC Identifier so that clients are not required to resubmit the same KYC records across multiple reporting entities. The Trap: Option B confuses CKYCR with FIU-IND. CKYCR handles the centralisation and de-duplication of KYC data and issuance of the KYC Identifier; FIU-IND handles intelligence on suspicious transactions. Options C and D describe licensing and criminal-records functions that are not part of CKYCR's mandate. Note: When a client provides a KYC Identifier, retrieve the records from CKYCR directly — do not require clients to resubmit documents already in the central registry unless the information has changed or is incomplete.
